label: Living systematic review protocol
framework: PRISMA-P structure with living review update methods

items.requirement: Identify the document as a living systematic review protocol.
items.prompt: What is the title and why should this review be living?
items.helpText: Living reviews are appropriate when evidence is emerging, uncertain, and decision-relevant.
items.exampleResponse: Living systematic review protocol: antiviral treatments for emerging respiratory infections.

items.prompt: What makes this topic high priority, rapidly evolving, and suitable for continuous updating?
items.helpText: Include evidence pace, uncertainty, policy relevance, and expected new studies.
items.exampleResponse: The evidence base is growing monthly and directly informs clinical and public health guidance.

items.prompt: What PICO question will be maintained over time?
items.helpText: The question should be stable enough for ongoing surveillance.
items.exampleResponse: Among adults with emerging respiratory infection, what is the effect of antiviral treatment on mortality, hospitalization, and adverse events?

items.requirement: State the review objectives clearly and in alignment with the review type.
items.prompt: What are the primary and secondary objectives this protocol will guide?
items.helpText: Objectives should match the review type: estimate, map, explain, synthesize experiences, compare reviews, or maintain living evidence. State objectives for maintaining up-to-date evidence and decision relevance over time.
items.exampleResponse: The primary objective is to synthesize the available evidence for the defined question. Secondary objectives include identifying gaps and describing implications for decision-makers.

items.prompt: What evidence, populations, contexts, concepts, interventions, outcomes, designs, dates, and languages will be included or excluded?
items.helpText: Make eligibility criteria explicit enough for consistent screening decisions. Define stable eligibility criteria and any rules for incorporating new evidence.
items.exampleResponse: We will include studies meeting the defined population, concept, context, evidence type, date range, and language criteria; exclusions will be documented with reasons.

items.prompt: Which databases, repositories, registers, websites, expert sources, and grey literature sources will be searched?
items.helpText: Information sources should fit the review type and include enough coverage to reduce avoidable bias. List databases, alerts, registries, preprint servers, and surveillance sources.
items.exampleResponse: We will search bibliographic databases, specialist registers, organizational repositories, relevant websites, and reference lists of included sources.

items.requirement: Describe search surveillance and update frequency.
items.prompt: How often will searches run, and what sources will be monitored for new evidence?
items.helpText: Living reviews need an explicit surveillance schedule.
items.exampleResponse: Database alerts, trial registries, and preprint servers will be monitored monthly, with full searches rerun every three months.

items.prompt: How will records or sources be screened and selected, and how will disagreements or uncertainty be handled?
items.helpText: Specify screening stages, reviewer numbers, piloting or calibration, software, reasons for exclusion, and documentation. Describe ongoing screening of newly identified records and update workflow.
items.exampleResponse: Screening criteria will be piloted. Records will be screened at title/abstract and full-text stages, with disagreements resolved by discussion or a third reviewer.

items.requirement: Describe extraction, coding, charting, or data transformation.
items.prompt: What data elements will be extracted or charted, and how will accuracy and consistency be checked?
items.helpText: Match the extraction fields to the review type and planned synthesis. Specify how new data will be extracted, verified, and merged with prior versions.
items.exampleResponse: A piloted form will capture bibliographic details, study characteristics, population/context, methods, findings, limitations, and fields needed for synthesis.

items.requirement: Describe critical appraisal, risk of bias, quality, relevance, or rigour assessment.
items.prompt: Will included evidence be appraised, which tools will be used, and how will appraisal affect interpretation?
items.helpText: Use tools appropriate to the included evidence and explain whether appraisal informs inclusion, sensitivity analysis, confidence, or interpretation. Describe ongoing risk-of-bias assessment for newly included studies.
items.exampleResponse: Two reviewers will apply design-appropriate appraisal tools, and results will be used to interpret confidence in the findings.

items.prompt: What new evidence will trigger screening, synthesis updates, certainty reassessment, or publication updates?
items.helpText: Triggers may include new trials, changed effect estimates, new safety signals, or guideline needs.
items.exampleResponse: A new randomized trial, serious safety signal, or change in certainty for a critical outcome will trigger an update.

items.requirement: Plan assessment of certainty, confidence, or credibility where relevant.
items.prompt: How will certainty, confidence, or credibility in the body of evidence or findings be assessed?
items.helpText: Use GRADE, GRADE-CERQual, review confidence ratings, or a justified alternative where applicable. Define how certainty will be reassessed when new evidence appears.
items.exampleResponse: Confidence will be assessed using a framework appropriate to the evidence type and reported alongside the main findings.

items.requirement: Define criteria for pausing or retiring living status.
items.prompt: When will the review stop being maintained as living?
items.helpText: Retirement criteria prevent indefinite maintenance commitments.
items.exampleResponse: Living status will be retired after 18 months without practice-changing evidence or when the topic is no longer a priority.

items.requirement: Describe ongoing screening, extraction, and appraisal workflow.
items.prompt: Who will monitor evidence, screen new records, extract data, appraise studies, and update analyses?
items.helpText: Living workflows need sustained responsibilities and handover plans.
items.exampleResponse: Two reviewers will screen monthly search results; the methods lead will verify extracted data and update meta-analyses.

items.prompt: How will users know when the review was last searched, updated, and changed?
items.helpText: Plan dated versions, change logs, and stable citations.
items.exampleResponse: Each public version will include last search date, change log, updated conclusions, and archived prior versions.

items.requirement: Identify appendices required for transparency and reproducibility.
items.prompt: Which appendices will be included to document methods and decisions?
items.helpText: Appendices may include search strategies, screening forms, extraction forms, appraisal tools, coding frameworks, stakeholder materials, and amendment logs. Include update log, surveillance strategy, version history, and retirement criteria.
items.exampleResponse: Appendices will include database search strategies, screening forms, extraction templates, appraisal tools, coding framework, and protocol amendments.
